rule: Conflicts a year are from the UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset, which begins in 1946. A conflict is one government against one opposing side over who governs or over territory, with 25 or more deaths in fighting that year; a movement fighting several governments counts as several conflicts, and one country can hold several. At war level means 1,000 or more deaths that year. Between states means the sides are states. Deaths by country and year are from UCDP's country-year file, which begins in 1989, in three parts: fighting between a state and an opponent, fighting between armed groups, and civilians killed deliberately, each with UCDP's low and high. UCDP places deaths in the country where they happened, so one war can appear in two countries. The label 'Israel and Palestine' is this page's name for UCDP's Israel row. A state that no longer exists is drawn on the shape that holds its capital today; a state that did not yet exist is counted in the one it was part of, so Eritrea's war before 1993 appears on Ethiopia and South Sudan's before 2011 on Sudan. UCDP revises recent years with each release; the last two are treated as provisional.
